sentences.en: My name is Helen Ouyang.
sentences.zh: 我叫海伦·欧阳。

sentences.en: I'm an emergency room doctor in New York City, and I've been fascinated by chronic pain for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我是纽约市的一名急诊科医生，长期以来一直对慢性疼痛很着迷。

sentences.en: When we touch a hot stove, we feel pain and pull our hand away.
sentences.zh: 当我们碰到热炉子时，会感到疼痛并缩回手。

sentences.en: This is our body's alarm system.
sentences.zh: 这是我们身体的警报系统。

sentences.en: But chronic pain is when the whole alarm system goes haywire.
sentences.zh: 但慢性疼痛是指整个警报系统出了故障。

sentences.en: The body is just in a state of alarm all the time, and we don't have any good treatments for that.
sentences.zh: 身体一直处于警报状态，而我们对此并没有什么好的治疗方法。

sentences.en: There's one incident that really sticks with me.
sentences.zh: 有一件事让我记忆犹新。

sentences.en: A man had driven to five different emergency rooms looking for his missing son, and it turned out actually that the son had died in our ER just about an hour earlier.
sentences.zh: 一名男子开车去了五家不同的急诊室寻找他失踪的儿子，结果发现他儿子大约一小时前就在我们的急诊室去世了。

sentences.en: The father explained how his son had undergone foot surgery and was prescribed Percocet.
sentences.zh: 这位父亲解释说，他儿子曾接受过足部手术，并被开了止痛药Percocet。

sentences.en: He got hooked and went on to use other drugs like heroin, which is what ultimately killed him.
sentences.zh: 他上瘾了，后来开始使用海洛因等其他毒品，这最终夺去了他的生命。

sentences.en: I heard recently that people were using virtual reality to treat chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 我最近听说人们正在使用虚拟现实技术来治疗慢性疼痛。

sentences.en: Around 50% of our brain is used in visual processing.
sentences.zh: 我们大脑中约50%的区域用于视觉处理。

sentences.en: So if you're wearing a headset that's totally immersive and bombarding you with visuals, then you can transport the brain to a new reality, possibly one without pain.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你戴上一款完全沉浸式并用视觉冲击你的头显，你就可以把大脑带入一个新的现实，一个可能没有疼痛的现实。

sentences.en: The first time I tried VR, I just stood in my living room and was moving around this fantastical world.
sentences.zh: 我第一次尝试VR时，就站在客厅里，在这个奇幻的世界里走动。

sentences.en: There were these canyon scenes with huge mountains and beaches, plants that grew into trees, that moved with the rhythm of my breathing.
sentences.zh: 那里有巨大的山脉和海滩，还有随着我的呼吸节奏而移动的植物长成的树木。

sentences.en: It was completely transporting.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉完全让人身临其境。

sentences.en: I reached out to a doctor named Brennan Spiegel at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center because I knew he was running one of the most comprehensive academic programs focused on VR.
sentences.zh: 我联系了西达赛奈医疗中心的布伦南·斯皮格尔医生，因为我知道他正在负责一个最全面的专注于VR的学术项目。

sentences.en: I watched him use virtual reality on his patients, and I saw how they had these deep, profound reactions, really unexpected ones.
sentences.zh: 我看着他将虚拟现实技术应用到病人身上，看到他们产生了深刻而强烈的反应，非常出人意料。

sentences.en: So here's my article, Can Virtual Reality Help Ease Chronic Pain?
sentences.zh: 这就是我的文章，《虚拟现实能帮助缓解慢性疼痛吗？》

sentences.en: After an hour and a half bus ride last November, Julia Monterosso arrived at a white Art Deco building in West Hollywood, just opposite a
sentences.zh: 去年11月，在经历了一个半小时的巴士车程后，朱莉娅·蒙特罗索抵达了西好莱坞一栋白色的装饰艺术风格建筑，就在

sentences.en: Chanel store and the Ivy, a restaurant famous for its celebrity sightings.
sentences.zh: 香奈儿专卖店和以常有名人出没而闻名的餐厅The Ivy对面。

sentences.en: Monterosso was there to see Brennan Spiegel, a gastroenterologist and researcher at Cedars-Sinai, who runs one of the
sentences.zh: 蒙特罗索是去见西达赛奈医疗中心的胃肠病学家兼研究员布伦南·斯皮格尔，他负责运营

sentences.en: largest academic medical initiatives studying virtual reality as a health therapy.
sentences.zh: 最大的研究虚拟现实作为健康疗法的学术医疗项目之一。

sentences.en: He started the program in 2015, after the hospital received a million-dollar donation from an investment banker on its board.
sentences.zh: 他在医院收到董事会一位投资银行家捐赠的一百万美元后，于2015年启动了这个项目。

sentences.en: Spiegel saw Monterosso in his clinic the week before and thought he might be able to
sentences.zh: 斯皮格尔前一周在诊所见过蒙特罗索，认为他或许能

sentences.en: help alleviate her symptoMs. Monterosso is 55 and petite, with youthful bangs and hair clipped back by tiny jeweled barrettes.
sentences.zh: 帮助减轻她的症状。蒙特罗索今年55岁，身材娇小，留着青春的刘海，头发用精致的珠宝发夹别在脑后。

sentences.en: Eighteen months earlier, pain seized her lower abdomen and never went away.
sentences.zh: 十八个月前，疼痛袭击了她的下腹部，从此再未消失。

sentences.en: After undergoing back surgery in September to treat a herniated disc, and after the constant ache in her abdomen worsened, she had to stop working as a house cleaner.
sentences.zh: 在九月份接受了椎间盘突出手术治疗后，腹部的持续疼痛反而加剧了，她不得不停止了清洁工的工作。

sentences.en: Eventually, following a series of tests that failed to reveal any clear cause, she landed in Spiegel's office.
sentences.zh: 最终，在进行了一系列未能查明明确病因的检查后，她来到了斯皮格尔的办公室。

sentences.en: She rated her pain an eight on a ten-point scale, with ten being the most severe.
sentences.zh: 她将自己的疼痛程度评为十分制中的八分，十分为最严重。

sentences.en: Chronic pain is generally defined as pain that has lasted three months or longer.
sentences.zh: 慢性疼痛通常被定义为持续三个月或更长时间的疼痛。

sentences.en: It is one of the leading causes of long-term disability in the world.
sentences.zh: 它是全球导致长期残疾的主要原因之一。

sentences.en: By some measures, 50 million Americans live with chronic pain, in part because the power of medicine to relieve pain remains woefully inadequate.
sentences.zh: 据某些统计，有5000万美国人患有慢性疼痛，部分原因是医学缓解疼痛的能力仍然极其不足。

sentences.en: As Daniel Claw, who runs the Chronic Pain and Fatigue
sentences.zh: 正如密歇根大学慢性疼痛与疲劳

sentences.en: Research Center at the University of Michigan, put it in a 2019 lecture, there isn't any drug in any chronic pain state that works in better than one out of three people.
sentences.zh: 研究中心负责人丹尼尔·克劳在2019年的一次讲座中所言，在任何慢性疼痛状态下，没有任何一种药物对超过三分之一的人有效。

sentences.en: He went on to say that non-pharmacological therapy should instead be front and center in managing chronic pain, rather than opioids, or for that matter, any of our drugs.
sentences.zh: 他接着说，非药物疗法应该在慢性疼痛管理中占据核心地位，而不是阿片类药物，或者就此而言，我们的任何药物。

sentences.en: Virtual reality is emerging as an unlikely tool for solving this intractable problem.
sentences.zh: 虚拟现实正在成为解决这一棘手问题的一种意想不到的工具。

sentences.en: The VR segment in healthcare alone, which according to some estimates is already valued at billions of dollars, is expected to grow by multiples of that in the next
sentences.zh: 仅医疗保健领域的VR细分市场，据估计价值已达数十亿美元，预计在未来

sentences.en: few years, with researchers seeing potential for it to help with everything from anxiety and
sentences.zh: 几年内将增长数倍，研究人员认为它在从焦虑和

sentences.en: depression, to rehabilitation after strokes, to surgeons strategizing where they will cut and stitch.
sentences.zh: 抑郁，到中风后的康复，再到外科医生规划切割和缝合位置等方面都有潜力。

sentences.en: In November, the Food and Drug Administration gave authorization for the first VR product to be marketed for the treatment of chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 11月，美国食品药品监督管理局批准了首款用于治疗慢性疼痛的VR产品上市。

sentences.en: Spiegel, who has the slim build of someone who runs
sentences.zh: 斯皮格尔有着马拉松运动员般的苗条身材——

sentences.en: marathons—he has finished 18 of them—fastened a black VR set onto Monterosso's head.
sentences.zh: 他已经完成了18场马拉松——他给蒙特罗索戴上了一副黑色VR头显。

sentences.en: It was wired to a computer, behind whose monitor sat Omir Laron, a psychiatrist and self-taught programmer who created the virtual worlds for this use.
sentences.zh: 它连接着一台电脑，显示器后面坐着奥米尔·拉隆，他是一位精神科医生兼自学成才的程序员，为这种用途创造了虚拟世界。

sentences.en: The beauty of doing everything here is that I can very quickly change things with patient feedback,
sentences.zh: 在这里做所有事情的好处是，我可以根据病人的反馈非常迅速地做出改变，

sentences.en: Laron told me.
sentences.zh: 拉隆告诉我。

sentences.en: If we outsourced it, it would be pretty much impossible, he said, or at least slow and expensive.
sentences.zh: 如果我们外包出去，那几乎是不可能的，他说，或者至少会很慢且昂贵。

sentences.en: The week before, Spiegel and Laron started collecting various biometric data from patients while they were in virtual reality.
sentences.zh: 前一周，斯皮格尔和拉隆开始在病人使用虚拟现实时收集各种生物识别数据。

sentences.en: Laron's computer showed what was happening to Monterosso's heart and eyes and to her cognitive load, or mental effort, while a two-dimensional version
sentences.zh: 拉隆的电脑显示了蒙特罗索的心脏、眼睛以及认知负荷（即心理努力）的变化，而另一块屏幕上则播放着

sentences.en: of what she was seeing in the headset played on another screen.
sentences.zh: 她在头显中看到的二维版本。

sentences.en: Monterosso sat in a plastic chair under fluorescent lights, but in virtual reality, she stood on a footbridge in a lush
sentences.zh: 蒙特罗索坐在荧光灯下的塑料椅子上，但在虚拟现实中，她站在一片郁郁葱葱的

sentences.en: foreSt. As she looked around at the giant trees, she trembled, and tears suddenly started streaming down her face.
sentences.zh: 森林中的人行天桥上。当她环顾四周巨大的树木时，她颤抖起来，眼泪突然夺眶而出。

sentences.en: Her cognitive load, shown as a pink line on the computer, started to increase.
sentences.zh: 她在电脑上显示的粉色线条代表的认知负荷开始增加。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm there with my son, she said in Spanish.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我和我儿子在一起，她用西班牙语说。

sentences.en: Her 21-year-old son died in a car accident in June.
sentences.zh: 她21岁的儿子在六月份的一场车祸中去世了。

sentences.en: They loved visiting Yosemite together, and in these virtual woods, she felt as if she were hiking with him again.
sentences.zh: 他们过去很喜欢一起去优胜美地旅游，在这些虚拟的树林里，她感觉就像又和他一起徒步旅行一样。

sentences.en: Spiegel reassured her that such intense reactions are very common, then leaned over to whisper to me, she's doing her own therapy right now.
sentences.zh: 斯皮格尔安慰她说这种强烈的反应很常见，然后俯身对我耳语道，她现在正在进行她自己的治疗。

sentences.en: As her tears dried, Monterosso slowly moved her head to look over a menu of choices.
sentences.zh: 当泪水干了之后，蒙特罗索慢慢转动头部查看菜单选项。

sentences.en: Selecting a beach scene option with her gaze, she found herself beside a placid sea, under a brilliant blue sky.
sentences.zh: 她用目光选择了一个海滩场景，发现自己置身于一片平静的大海旁，头顶是灿烂的蓝天。

sentences.en: A mandala moved toward and away from her, sinking her breathing rates to a relaxation-inducing tempo.
sentences.zh: 一个曼陀罗图案向她靠近又远离，将她的呼吸频率调整到诱导放松的节奏。

sentences.en: Her cognitive load and heart rate slowed, and her pupils became less dilated, all signs of relaxation.
sentences.zh: 她的认知负荷和心率减慢，瞳孔扩张程度降低，这些都是放松的迹象。

sentences.en: After a while, she headed to the mountains, where goats trotted by.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，她前往山间，那里有山羊跑过。

sentences.en: Welcome back, Spiegel said as Monterosso removed the headset.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来，斯皮格尔在蒙特罗索摘下头显时说道。

sentences.en: He pulled up some of her measurements on the computer monitor.
sentences.zh: 他在电脑显示器上调出她的一些测量数据。

sentences.en: He explained that larger pupils, for example, indicate stress.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，例如，瞳孔变大表示压力。

sentences.en: In the forest, they're big.
sentences.zh: 在森林里，它们很大。

sentences.en: Because my emotions were very strong then, Monterosso replied.
sentences.zh: 因为那时我的情绪非常强烈，蒙特罗索回答。

sentences.en: In the mountains, the pupils were smaller because you were relaxed.
sentences.zh: 在山里，瞳孔变小了，因为你放松了。

sentences.en: Spiegel continued, his finger tracing a downward-sloping line on the screen.
sentences.zh: 斯皮格尔继续说道，手指在屏幕上划过一条向下倾斜的线。

sentences.en: I've tried breathing exercises before, she said, but this is much more relaxing.
sentences.zh: 我以前试过呼吸练习，她说，但这要放松得多。

sentences.en: She rubbed her abdomen.
sentences.zh: 她揉了揉腹部。

sentences.en: I don't have pain in my stomach now.
sentences.zh: 我现在胃里不疼了。

sentences.en: Next, Monterosso entered another virtual environment that Leron built specifically for patients with chronic gastrointestinal symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 接下来，蒙特罗索进入了拉隆专门为患有慢性胃肠道症状的病人构建的另一个虚拟环境。

sentences.en: In this setting, unlike the previous one, Monterosso used hand controls.
sentences.zh: 在这个场景中，与前一个不同，蒙特罗索使用了手持控制器。

sentences.en: Inside a virtual clinic, a robot named Maya, short for Mixed Reality Artificial Intelligence Assistant, guided her to a young
sentences.zh: 在一个虚拟诊所里，一个名叫玛雅（Maya，混合现实人工智能助手的缩写）的机器人引导她走向一位年轻的

sentences.en: blonde woman who expressed frustration with abdominal symptoMs. Monterosso examined the patient with her
sentences.zh: 金发女性，她表达了对腹部症状的沮丧。蒙特罗索用她的

sentences.en: virtual hands, placing a stethoscope on her stomach to listen to the sounds of digestion.
sentences.zh: 虚拟双手检查了病人，将听诊器放在她的肚子上听消化声。

sentences.en: Maya explained how the brain and the gut worked together.
sentences.zh: 玛雅解释了大脑和肠道是如何协同工作的。

sentences.en: As she spoke, an image of a brain popped up, connected to intestines by a yellow flashing line.
sentences.zh: 当她说话时，大脑的图像弹了出来，通过一条闪烁的黄色线条与肠道相连。

sentences.en: When the brain became stressed, it turned fuchsia in color, and the yellow line to the gut metamorphosed into a stream of fire.
sentences.zh: 当大脑感到压力时，它变成了紫红色，连接肠道的黄色线条变成了火流。

sentences.en: A pounding heart appeared.
sentences.zh: 一颗跳动的心脏出现了。

sentences.en: Because the program is in English, Spiegel translated Maya's speech into Spanish.
sentences.zh: 由于程序是英文的，斯皮格尔将玛雅的话翻译成了西班牙语。

sentences.en: When you have a lot of stress, the heart beats faster, the intestines can move faster, and oxygen in the body goes to the brain, away from your intestines.
sentences.zh: 当你压力很大时，心脏跳动加快，肠道运动可能加快，身体里的氧气流向大脑，远离你的肠道。

sentences.en: This really helped me to understand how the brain and the intestines work together.
sentences.zh: 这真的帮助我理解了大脑和肠道是如何协同工作的。

sentences.en: Because after the accident of my son, I've been very sad, Monterosso told Spiegel after her VR session.
sentences.zh: 因为在我儿子出事后，我一直很伤心，蒙特罗索在VR疗程结束后告诉斯皮格尔。

sentences.en: She looked around the room, seemingly surprised to see everyone.
sentences.zh: 她环顾房间，似乎对看到大家感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I didn't even notice the people here, she said.
sentences.zh: 我甚至没注意到这里的人，她说。

sentences.en: That's because people can't live in two realities at once, Spiegel said.
sentences.zh: 那是因为人不能同时生活在两个现实中，斯皮格尔说。

sentences.en: He was describing VR's unique ability to convey a sense of just being there, wherever there happens to be.
sentences.zh: 他描述的是VR独特的能力，即传达一种“身临其境”的感觉，无论“那里”是什么地方。

sentences.en: As he puts it in his book, VRX, How Virtual Therapeutics Will Revolutionize Medicine.
sentences.zh: 正如他在他的书《VRX：虚拟疗法将如何彻底改变医学》中所写的那样。

sentences.en: All of its revolutionary potential tumbles out of its ability to compel a person's brain and body to react to a different reality.
sentences.zh: 它所有的革命性潜力都源于它能够迫使人的大脑和身体对一个不同的现实做出反应。

sentences.en: Humans may use roughly 50% of our brains in visual processing, Spiegel writes.
sentences.zh: 人类大脑中大约50%的区域用于视觉处理，斯皮格尔写道。

sentences.en: So bombard the eyes with spectacular and dynamic visions, and next thing you know, those 3 billion
sentences.zh: 所以用壮观且动态的视觉画面轰炸眼睛，接下来你会发现，那每秒30亿次的

sentences.en: neuronal firings per second will ricochet through half the brain to process the overwhelming load of visual data.
sentences.zh: 神经元放电将穿过半个大脑，以处理海量的视觉数据。

sentences.en: In this reality, Monterosso no longer experienced pain.
sentences.zh: 在这个现实中，蒙特罗索不再感到疼痛。

sentences.en: What we saw today with Julio was like a cyberdelic, as if she took a psilocybin, Spiegel told me, referring to the hallucinogen.
sentences.zh: 我们今天在朱莉娅身上看到的就像一种‘赛博迷幻’，就好像她服用了裸盖菇素一样，斯皮格尔指着那种致幻剂对我说道。

sentences.en: She had explosive insights into how to modify her own life.
sentences.zh: 她对如何改变自己的生活有了爆发性的洞察。

sentences.en: Her amygdala was on fire, he added, referring to the almond-shaped structure in the brain that processes emotions.
sentences.zh: 她的杏仁核在燃烧，他补充道，指的是大脑中处理情绪的杏仁状结构。

sentences.en: The real-time bio-data helped her connect the dots between brain and body, while Maya taught her how she could potentially turn the pain off.
sentences.zh: 实时生物数据帮助她连接了大脑和身体之间的点，而玛雅则教她如何潜在地关闭疼痛。

sentences.en: Even though Spiegel tried to explain all this to her the week before, she did not grasp it until she tried VR.
sentences.zh: 尽管斯皮格尔前一周试图向她解释这一切，但直到尝试了VR，她才真正领悟。

sentences.en: I almost don't even care what the mechanism is of how it's working, Spiegel told me.
sentences.zh: 我几乎不在乎它是通过什么机制起作用的，斯皮格尔告诉我。

sentences.en: And indeed, its impact on chronic pain still isn't fully understood.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它对慢性疼痛的影响仍未被完全理解。

sentences.en: What really matters to him is the answer to his question, is it clinically working or not?
sentences.zh: 对他来说，真正重要的是他问题的答案：它在临床上是否有效？

sentences.en: I began looking into novel treatments for chronic pain because, as an emergency room doctor, I've long grappled with caring for patients at the extremes of persistent suffering.
sentences.zh: 我开始研究治疗慢性疼痛的新方法，因为作为一名急诊科医生，我长期以来一直在努力照顾那些处于持续痛苦极端状态的病人。

sentences.en: I've seen what happens when our medical treatments turn deadly.
sentences.zh: 我见过我们的医疗手段变成致命武器时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Years after telling a man that his son had died of an opioid overdose, which resulted from an addiction
sentences.zh: 在告诉一名男子他的儿子死于阿片类药物过量（源于足部手术后对处方止痛药的成瘾）多年后，

sentences.en: to prescription painkillers following foot surgery, I can still hear his wails and recall how they brought my hospital's bustling ER to near silence.
sentences.zh: 我依然能听到他的哀嚎，并记得它们是如何让医院繁忙的急诊室陷入近乎死寂的。

sentences.en: The opioid epidemic, an American tragedy, has no clear end in sight.
sentences.zh: 阿片类药物流行，这一美国悲剧，目前还看不到明确的终点。

sentences.en: Drug overdose deaths, most of them from opioids, rose 30% during the first year of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 药物过量死亡人数（其中大部分来自阿片类药物）在疫情第一年上升了30%。

sentences.en: While illicit fentanyl is largely to blame, the healthcare system is also complicit in this harrowing statistic.
sentences.zh: 虽然非法芬太尼在很大程度上是罪魁祸首，但医疗保健系统也对这一令人痛心的统计数据负有责任。

sentences.en: At one point, 80% of those who were using heroin first misused prescription opioids.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，80%的海洛因使用者最初都是滥用处方阿片类药物。

sentences.en: Patient-rated pain scores in Siren Red used to be a regular feature on my ER's dashboard, having gained the same importance as other vital signs like oxygen levels and blood
sentences.zh: 急诊室仪表盘上曾经定期显示病人自评疼痛评分，其重要性与氧气水平和血压等其他生命体征相当，

sentences.en: pressure, until they quickly disappeared after Purdue Pharma became implicated in the unethical marketing of opioids.
sentences.zh: 直到普渡制药因不道德的阿片类药物营销被曝光后，这些评分很快就消失了。

sentences.en: The healthcare system, confronted with evidence that these drugs were being over-prescribed and even harming some patients, then began cutting them off abruptly in some cases,
sentences.zh: 医疗系统在面对这些药物被过度开具甚至伤害了一些病人的证据时，开始在某些情况下突然切断供应，

sentences.en: instead of tapering their use or offering alternative treatments.
sentences.zh: 而不是逐步减少用量或提供替代疗法。

sentences.en: The patients who haunt me nearly as much as those who have succumbed to the opioid crisis are the ones I send away, often in as much pain as when they first arrived.
sentences.zh: 那些让我魂牵梦绕的病人，几乎和那些死于阿片类危机的人一样多，他们是我送走的病人，离开时往往和刚来时一样痛苦。

sentences.en: When I meet patients with chronic pain in the ER, they narrate their years of suffering, and I respond with remedies that I know, and they know that I know, they've tried before
sentences.zh: 当我在急诊室遇到慢性疼痛患者时，他们讲述着多年的痛苦，而我回应的是我知道（他们也知道我知道）他们以前尝试过却毫无效果的疗法。

sentences.en: with no success.
sentences.zh: 这就是我作为医生感到最无力的时候。

sentences.en: This is when I feel the most futility as a physician.
sentences.zh: 搞清楚慢性疼痛对医生来说可能令人困惑。

sentences.en: Figuring out chronic pain can be mystifying for doctors.
sentences.zh: 在人们脊柱的核磁共振研究中，在那些报告没有感到任何疼痛的受试者中，有一半人被发现有椎间盘突出。

sentences.en: In MRI studies of people's spines, disc herniations have been found in half of those subjects who nevertheless report feeling no pain.
sentences.zh: 与年龄相关的退行性发现也显示与症状的相关性很小。一些膝关节骨关节炎患者在关节置换手术后仍然感到疼痛。

sentences.en: Age-related degenerative findings also show little correlation with symptoMs. Some patients with knee osteoarthritis continue to have pain after joint replacement surgery.
sentences.zh: 虽然慢性疼痛可能会让常规扫描和检查束手无策，但这种情况是非常真实的，造成了无法估量的痛苦。

sentences.en: While chronic pain may flummox the usual scans and tests, the condition is very much real, causing immeasurable suffering.
sentences.zh: 我们至少已经认识到，由组织损伤引起的急性疼痛与慢性疼痛不同，后者现在被认为是一种独立的疾病。

sentences.en: We have at least come to recognize that acute pain resulting from damage to tissues is not the same as chronic pain, which is now considered a distinct disease.
sentences.zh: 我们是如何得出这一认识的，可以追溯到20世纪80年代初在伦敦进行的一项偶然实验。

sentences.zh: 在沃尔的实验室里，研究人员对大鼠的后腿施加疼痛刺激。

sentences.en: The animals developed large fields of pain that could easily be activated months later with a light tap or gentle warmth, even in spots that weren't being touched directly.
sentences.zh: 这些动物产生了广泛的痛觉区域，即便在数月后，只需轻触或给予温和的热刺激，甚至在并未直接接触的部位，这些痛觉也能轻易被激活。

sentences.en: I was changing the function of the nervous system, such that its properties were altered, Wolf says.
sentences.zh: 沃尔说：“我改变了神经系统的功能，使其属性发生了变化。”

sentences.en: Pain was not simply a measure of some peripheral pathology, he concluded.
sentences.zh: 他得出结论，疼痛不仅仅是某种外周病理的衡量标准。

sentences.en: It could also be the consequence of abnormal amplification within the nervous system.
sentences.zh: 它也可能是神经系统内部异常放大的结果。

sentences.en: This was the phenomenon of central sensitization.
sentences.zh: 这就是中枢敏化现象。

sentences.en: Before this discovery, he says, the feeling was always pain is a symptom that reflects a disease, and now we know that pain often is a consequence
sentences.zh: 他说，在这一发现之前，人们总是认为疼痛是反映疾病的一种症状，而现在我们知道，疼痛往往是

sentences.en: of a diseased state of the nervous system itself.
sentences.zh: 神经系统自身病变状态的结果。

sentences.en: Some ailments, like rheumatoid arthritis, can exhibit both peripheral pathology and central sensitization.
sentences.zh: 类风湿性关节炎等一些疾病，既表现出外周病理，也表现出中枢敏化。

sentences.en: Others, like fibromyalgia, characterized by pain throughout the body, are considered solely a problem of the central nervous system itself.
sentences.zh: 而纤维肌痛等其他疾病，其特征是全身性疼痛，被认为完全是中枢神经系统自身的问题。

sentences.en: A better grasp of how chronic pain changes the central nervous system has emerged since Wolf's experiment.
sentences.zh: 自沃尔的实验以来，人们对慢性疼痛如何改变中枢神经系统有了更深入的了解。

sentences.zh: 西北大学阿瓦尼亚·阿普卡里安的疼痛实验室发现，当背痛

sentences.en: persists, the activity in the brain shifts from the sensory and motor regions to the areas associated with emotion, which include the amygdala and the hippocampus.
sentences.zh: 持续存在时，大脑的活动会从感觉和运动区域转移到与情绪相关的区域，包括杏仁核和海马体。

sentences.en: It's now part of the internal psychology,
sentences.zh: 阿普卡里安说，这现在成了内在心理的一部分，

sentences.en: Apkaryan says, a negative emotional cloud that takes hold.
sentences.zh: 一种挥之不去的负面情绪阴云。

sentences.en: The brain itself morphs.
sentences.zh: 大脑本身发生了形变。

sentences.en: Patients with chronic pain can show a significant loss of gray matter in the prefrontal cortex, the attention and decision-making
sentences.zh: 慢性疼痛患者的前额叶皮层（大脑中负责注意力和决策的区域，位于前额后方）以及负责传递感觉信号的丘脑，

sentences.en: region of the brain that sits behind our foreheads, as well as in the thalamus, which relays sensory signals.
sentences.zh: 其灰质会显著减少。

sentences.en: Both areas are important in processing pain.
sentences.zh: 这两个区域在处理疼痛方面都很重要。

sentences.en: Excitatory neurotransmitters increase and inhibitory ones decrease, while glial and other immune cells drive inflammation.
sentences.zh: 兴奋性神经递质增加，抑制性神经递质减少，同时神经胶质细胞和其他免疫细胞会引发炎症。

sentences.en: The nervous system, unbalanced, magnifies and prolongs the pain.
sentences.zh: 失去平衡的神经系统会放大并延长疼痛。

sentences.en: The system goes haywire, like an alarm that keeps blaring even when there's no threat, even when the pain isn't protective anymore.
sentences.zh: 系统陷入了混乱，就像一个警报器，即使在没有威胁、疼痛不再具有保护作用时，依然响个不停。

sentences.en: Instead, it just begets more pain.
sentences.zh: 相反，它只会招致更多的疼痛。

sentences.en: And the longer it lasts, the more deeply systemic it becomes and the harder it is to resolve.
sentences.zh: 而且持续时间越长，它就越深入系统，也越难解决。

sentences.zh: 神经科学界有一句流行的话：神经元一起放电，就会连接在一起。

sentences.zh: 这是神经可塑性在实践中的一个例子。

sentences.en: But if our brains really are plastic, what is shaped there can be reshaped.
sentences.zh: 但如果大脑确实具有可塑性，那么其中塑造的东西也可以被重塑。

sentences.zh: 那些针对大脑而非疼痛的背部或膝盖的疗法，无论是通过心理学、药物、大脑直接刺激还是虚拟现实，

sentences.zh: 理论上都可以消除慢性疼痛。

sentences.en: Nobody was using virtual reality to reduce the pain of patients before us, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说：“在我们之前，没有人使用虚拟现实来减轻患者的疼痛。”

sentences.zh: 当时，在2017年春天，Applied VR专注于治疗那些必须接受医院手术的患者（尤其是儿童）的焦虑和急性疼痛。

sentences.zh: 他被迷住了。

sentences.zh: 两个月后，他戒掉了麻醉止痛药。

sentences.zh: 杰斯特最近告诉我：“现在，当疼痛来袭时，我会立即使用这种训练。”

sentences.en: He started charting his opioid use in a little blue notebook while continuing daily VR sessions.
sentences.zh: 他紧闭双眼，深吸了一口气。

sentences.zh: “我可以让自己重新集中注意力一分钟，”他说，想象着其中一种特殊的VR植物，当他的呼吸平稳缓慢时，

sentences.zh: 其光秃秃的树枝会变得枝繁叶茂，这由头显上的传感器检测到。

sentences.en: He squeezed his eyes closed and breathed in deeply.
sentences.zh: 当萨克曼和他的联合创始人马修·斯托特听说杰斯特通过VR成功戒除阿片类药物后，他们重新设计了产品，

sentences.en: I can refocus myself for a minute, he said, imagining one of the special VR plants whose bare branches become full of leaves when his breathing

sentences.en: is slow and steady, as detected by a sensor on the headset.
sentences.zh: 贝丝·达内尔，心理学家兼斯坦福大学疼痛缓解创新实验室主任，是该公司的首席科学顾问。

sentences.en: When Sackman and his co-founder,
sentences.zh: 她将这种呼吸驱动的树描述为一种让视觉元素向用户反馈其自身生理变化的方式。

sentences.en: Matthew Stout, heard about Jester's success with VR and opioid tapering, they redesigned their product,

sentences.en: Beth Darnell, a psychologist and director of Stanford's Pain Relief Innovations Lab, is the company's chief science advisor.
sentences.zh: 斯皮格尔和勒隆用图表捕捉到的那种生物识别数据，在这里被提炼成一种美观的格式，

sentences.zh: 在不打断患者虚拟现实沉浸感的情况下，提供即时、可操作的反馈。

sentences.zh: 因为杰斯特把头显留在了他进行物理治疗的设施里，他在疫情期间有一年多无法使用它。

sentences.en: It's a powerful way to teach principles and concepts that extend well beyond what we do in traditional didactic cognitive behavioral therapy.
sentences.zh: 但他发现自己记住了在VR中学到的课程。

sentences.en: The sort of biometric data that Spiegel and Leron captured with their graphs are here distilled into an aesthetically appealing format that delivers

sentences.en: immediate, actionable feedback without interrupting a patient's immersion in virtual reality.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，正如华盛顿大学教授霍夫曼所指出的：“我们绝对可以在你戴着头显时减轻你的疼痛，但你不可能整天待在里面。”

sentences.en: Because Jester left his headset at the facility where he did physical therapy, he was unable to use it for more than a year during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: Reliever还拥有一些模块，提示患者通过游戏重新引导注意力，

sentences.zh: 平均每次疗程持续七分钟，患者被要求在八周内每天只做一次。

sentences.en: After all, as Hoffman, the University of Washington professor, points out, We can definitely reduce your pain while you're in the helmet, but you can't stay in there all day.
sentences.zh: 与游戏界流行的VR不同，Reliever只追踪患者的头部运动，这意味着杰斯特无法走到树前去抓树枝，也无法赶走牛。

sentences.en: The average session lasts seven minutes, and patients are directed to do just one a day for eight weeks.
sentences.zh: 托德·马多克斯，认知神经科学家兼Applied VR研发副总裁，用一个例子解释了Reliever的工作原理。

sentences.en: Unlike the sort of VR that's popular in gaming, Reliever tracks only patients' head movements, meaning Jester can't go up to the tree and grab a branch, or chase cows away.
sentences.zh: “我用一棵茁壮成长的树来奖励你，因为你产生了适当的呼吸模式。”

sentences.en: The product is designed to be easier to use than an iPhone.
sentences.zh: “我没有让你阅读PDF或在脑中计数。”

sentences.en: You just strap on the headset and press the power button.
sentences.zh: 但通过使用VR让大脑参与体验式学习，他说，

sentences.zh: “我已经让你走上了行为改变的道路。”

sentences.en: I am rewarding you with a tree that flourishes for generating an appropriate breathing pattern.
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，Applied VR已筹集了超过7000万美元。

sentences.en: I didn't tell you to read a PDF or count in your head.
sentences.zh: 大部分资金已用于产品开发和临床试验。

sentences.en: But by using VR to engage the brain in experiential learning, he says,
sentences.zh: 一项由该公司附属研究人员最近发表的研究报告称，他们在疫情期间通过Facebook广告和疼痛组织招募了受试者，

sentences.en: I have just set you on a path for behavioral change.
sentences.zh: Reliever组的慢性背痛平均下降了近43%，而对照组为25%。

sentences.en: To date, Applied VR has raised more than $70 million.
sentences.zh: 对于使用Reliever的人来说，疼痛对他们的活动和睡眠的干扰也减少了。

sentences.en: Much of this money has been directed toward product development and clinical trials.
sentences.zh: 在最后一次VR疗程三个月后，这些改善大多被发现是持久的，有时甚至持续了六个月。

sentences.en: A recently published study by researchers affiliated with the company, for which they recruited subjects during the pandemic through Facebook ads and pain organizations,
sentences.zh: 如果这些数据成立，它们将表明用户保留了他们在虚拟世界中学到的应对技能，就像杰斯特那样。

sentences.en: reported an average drop in chronic back pain by nearly 43% for the Reliever group, compared with 25% for the control group.
sentences.zh: 马多克斯假设该程序改变了大脑的结构和功能。

sentences.en: For those who used Reliever, pain also interfered less with their activity and sleep.
sentences.zh: 虽然承认他没有具体的证据，但他表示：

sentences.zh: “没有大脑的变化，就不会有患者报告结果的变化。”

sentences.en: If these numbers hold up, they would indicate that users had retained the coping skills they learned inside the virtual world, as Jester did.
sentences.zh: 11月中旬，FDA授权Applied VR将现在的Reliever用于慢性下背痛，

sentences.en: Maddox hypothesizes that the program alters structure and function of the brain.
sentences.zh: 这是一个监管上的先例，可能为该机构批准类似的VR产品铺平道路。

sentences.en: While acknowledging that he does not have concrete evidence, he says,
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是因为与药物相比，其副作用微乎其微。

sentences.en: You don't get changes in patient-reported outcomes without changes in the brain.
sentences.zh: FDA的一位高级官员告诉我，医疗器械监管不是药物监管。

sentences.en: In mid-November, the FDA gave Applied VR authorization to market what is now Reliever for chronic lower back pain,
sentences.zh: “对于VR，我们需要在某些技术和用途上市前进行审查，但我们也可以设想，有些情况下这是不必要的。”

sentences.en: a regulatory first that may pave the way for the agency to okay similar VR products.

sentences.en: In large part because the side effects are minimal compared with those of pharmaceuticals.
sentences.zh: 萨克曼声称他们的背景给了他们优势。

sentences.zh: 他说，当他了解VR时，他问的第一个问题是：“如果这东西这么强大，为什么它还待在学术实验室里？”

sentences.en: For VR, some of those technologies and some of the uses we need to see before they can be marketed, but we can also envision and imagine there are some where that's not necessary.
sentences.zh: “为什么没有更多人知道它？”

sentences.zh: “为什么人们不在临床实践中使用它？”

sentences.zh: 他自己回答了这些问题。

sentences.en: The first questions he says he asked when he learned about VR were, If this stuff is so powerful, why is it sitting in an academic lab?
sentences.zh: “这是因为没有人将其产品化。”

sentences.zh: 西达赛奈医学中心的勒隆承认了这一点。

sentences.en: He answered the questions himself.
sentences.zh: “我们不是商人，”他告诉我。

sentences.en: It's because there aren't people productizing it.
sentences.zh: 他和斯皮格尔打算将他们自己的VR产品留在内部。

sentences.en: There's not a business model.
sentences.zh: “我们在这里赚钱的方式是拨款。”

sentences.en: Leron, at Cedars-Sinai, concedes the point.
sentences.zh: “那是我们的货币，”斯皮格尔说。

sentences.en: We aren't businessmen, he told me.
sentences.zh: “我不希望它突然被商业化出售和授权，导致我无法再获得NIH的拨款。”

sentences.zh: 斯皮格尔说，除了2016年的一笔小额一次性付款外，他并没有从Applied VR公司赚取任何钱，但他偶尔会为该公司提供咨询，

sentences.zh: 一位医疗技术分析师。

sentences.zh: 你已经尝试过其他所有方法了。

sentences.en: In January, as COVID cases soared again, a man in his late 50s with chronic back pain came into the
sentences.zh: 一月份，随着新冠病例再次激增，一位 50 多岁、患有慢性背痛的男子来到了我工作的

sentences.en: ER where I work.
sentences.zh: 急诊室。

sentences.en: His painkillers were no longer providing relief.
sentences.zh: 他的止痛药已不再起作用了。

sentences.en: He was unsure if they ever really helped.
sentences.zh: 他不确定这些药是否真的有帮助。

sentences.en: But everything seemed worse now, he said.
sentences.zh: 但他表示，现在一切似乎都更糟了。

sentences.en: He had been unable to travel.
sentences.zh: 他一直无法出门旅行。

sentences.en: He was stuck in his apartment, in pain.
sentences.zh: 他被困在公寓里，忍受着痛苦。

sentences.en: His doctor's appointments scrambled with each pandemic surge.
sentences.zh: 随着疫情的每一次激增，他的医生预约都被打乱了。

sentences.en: I told him all I could do was order a different formulation of one of his medicines, a desperate and often useless step that doctors take when trying to alleviate chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他，我能做的只是为他开另一种配方的药物，这是医生在试图缓解慢性疼痛时采取的一种绝望且往往无用的措施。

sentences.en: But he had come with an idea of his own.
sentences.zh: 但他自己有一个想法。

sentences.en: Have you heard of people using virtual reality for pain?
sentences.zh: 你听说过有人用虚拟现实来治疗疼痛吗？

sentences.en: He asked me eagerly.
sentences.zh: 他急切地问我。

sentences.en: How can I get that?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么得到那个？
